Nikhil and Farhan have given us good context on the inbound call centre operations. Today we want to understand the Compliance Calling function — what it is, what data is involved, and how it flows downstream. [00:00:22] Deepa Lakshmi: Hi Rohan, Priya. Happy to help. Compliance Calling is a bit different from the regular call centre. We don't take inbound calls. We make outbound calls to existing customers for verification purposes. [00:00:36] Rohan Desai: Walk us through what Compliance Calling actually entails. [00:00:40] Deepa Lakshmi: So we call it Compliance Calling or sometimes Hygiene Calling. The purpose is to verify that the loan was originated properly and that the customer's information is accurate. Think of it as a quality check on the lending process. [00:00:55] Deepa Lakshmi: There are four types of compliance calls we make: Type 1 is a Pre-Disbursement Verification call. Before the loan amount is disbursed, we call the customer to confirm they actually applied for the loan, they know the terms, they've met the branch staff, and everything is above board. This is a fraud prevention measure. Type 2 is Post-Disbursement. Within a week of the loan being disbursed, we call to confirm the customer received the funds, confirm the loan amount and EMI, and check if the customer has any concerns. Type 3 is a Welcome Call. This is more of a relationship call — we welcome the customer, explain how to reach customer care, tell them about the app, explain their EMI schedule. Type 4 is a Periodic Hygiene Check. These happen at random intervals during the loan tenure. We verify the customer's contact details are still current, ask if they've had any issues, check if they've been asked for any unofficial payments by branch staff. [00:01:55] Rohan Desai: That's quite structured. For each of these call types, what data do you collect? [00:02:01] Deepa Lakshmi: Each call type has a questionnaire. The questions are different for each type. My team makes the call, asks the questions, and fills in the answers. [00:02:12] Rohan Desai: Where are the answers recorded? [00:02:15] Deepa Lakshmi: In Excel. We have a master Excel file per month. Each row is one call. The columns include the customer's name, loan account number, mobile number, date of call, call type, and then the individual question responses. The questionnaire varies by type but for example, the Pre-Disbursement one asks things like: "Did you visit the branch?", "Did you meet the loan officer?", "Were you explained the terms of the loan?", "Was any unofficial payment requested?", "Are you aware of your EMI amount and tenure?" [00:02:50] Rohan Desai: Is the customer informed at the start of the call that their responses will be recorded and may be shared with other teams? [00:02:57] Deepa Lakshmi: We identify ourselves as calling from the company and state the purpose of the call — that we're calling for verification. But we don't give a formal data privacy notice or say anything about how the data will be used or shared. [00:03:12] Rohan Desai: And these calls, are they recorded in Ameyo like the inbound calls? This is a fraud prevention measure. Type 2 is Post-Disbursement. Within a week of the loan being disbursed, we call to confirm the customer received the funds, confirm the loan amount and EMI, and check if the customer has any concerns. Type 3 is a Welcome Call. This is more of a relationship call — we welcome the customer, explain how to reach customer care, tell them about the app, explain their EMI schedule. Type 4 is a Periodic Hygiene Check. These happen at random intervals during the loan tenure. We verify the customer's contact details are still current, ask if they've had any issues, check if they've been asked for any unofficial payments by branch staff.
